title: Parallel scaling 1..N cores at 0.85x linear at n greater equal 28
description:
Measure parallel scaling of `permanent_bipedal3_parallel` (T15) on the dev host across rayon thread counts 1..N (N = physical core count); scaling factor $\ge 0.85\times$ per physical core for $n \ge 28$.

## Background

CLAUDE.md success criterion 5 / epic success criterion 5: parallel scaling is $\ge 0.85\times$ per physical core up to the host's physical core count, for $n \ge 28$ (the regime where work-per-subset overcomes scheduler overhead). The dev host is AMD Ryzen 9 5900X with 12 physical cores.

This sim sweeps thread counts $T \in \{1, 2, 4, 8, 12\}$ at $n \in \{28, 32, 36\}$ and reports speedup ratios.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] CSV at `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/s2_parallel_scaling-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` records mean wall-clock vs thread count for $n \in \{28, 32, 36\}$ on the dev host.
- [ ] [hard] For $n \in \{28, 32, 36\}$ and $T \in \{2, 4, 8, 12\}$: scaling factor $\frac{T_1}{T \cdot T_T} \ge 0.85$ (within 95% CI).
- [ ] [hard] Hardware fingerprint, rayon thread pool config, and RNG seed are recorded.
- [ ] [hard] Writeup at `dev/plans/s2_parallel_scaling.md` exists, attached via `jit doc add`.
- [ ] [hard] Determinism: output value across thread counts is bit-identical (same RNG seed).
